title: every instrument in the coverage space starts from a ROW, so a test file no row cites is invisible to all of them -- 151 of 279, uncounted and unowned
body:
**THE ESTATE GATES ONE DIRECTION OF ROW-TO-ARTEFACT AGREEMENT AND HAS NEVER COUNTED THE OTHER.** A row citing an artefact is checked. An artefact no row cites is not, and **the instrument nearest to it says so about itself, in its own words:**

    declared_kind_check.sh:247
      It cannot see an ORPHANED artefact at a path no row cites, which is the
      other end of the same defect

The same sentence appears in its roster row in `runner_roster_check.sh`. **The gap is NAMED and it is not OWNED, and those are different things** -- which is `AC-00.16`'s second conjunct exactly: instruments declare their reach, AND something names what the union does not cover. Naming it in the reach line of the tool that cannot see it is not the same as measuring it.

## THE POPULATION, DERIVED 2026-09-05 17:43Z

    find native/rust -path '*/tests/*.rs' -not -path '*/target/*' | sort > exist
    jq -r '.tests[]? | select(.file? != null) | .file' intent/.canon/st/*.json | sort -u > cited
    comm -23 exist cited

| quantity | count |
| --- | --- |
| test files on disk (`*/tests/*.rs`, excluding `target/`) | **279** |
| distinct paths cited by an AT row's `file` | 223 |
| **on disk, cited by NO row** | **151** |

**THE CORPUS MOVES WHENEVER ANY NODE COMMITS.** These are a measurement with a timestamp, not properties. Re-derive rather than quote; the instrument above is the deliverable, not the table.

### Both control arms fired, on the same machinery

- `remedies_are_reachable.rs` is cited (`AT-06.11`) and is **NOT** in the orphan set.
- `routing_is_opt_in.rs` **IS** in the orphan set and is cited by nothing -- the instance that raised this.

## THE 151 IS NOT THE DEFECT COUNT, AND SAYING SO IS THE POINT OF THIS ROW

**IT IS NOT A CLAIM THAT THE ESTATE IS MISSING 151 ACCEPTANCE ROWS.** Most of those files were never meant to be acceptance witnesses. **The finding is that NOTHING IN THE ESTATE CAN TELL YOU WHICH ONES SHOULD BE**, and no instrument is even counting the set.

There is a sharper sub-population, and it uses the estate's OWN coverage mechanism rather than one invented here. `contract.rs` L3: *the cited file carries the AT's id, literally* -- chosen because it is checkable from both ends and survives rewording, where a cited test NAME survives neither.

| of the 151 orphans | count |
| --- | --- |
| **declare an `AT-NN.N` id inside their own text** | **36** |
| declare none | 115 |
| are helper modules (`tests/common/mod.rs`) rather than targets | 3 |

**THOSE 36 ASSERT COVERAGE FROM ONE END WHILE THE CANON POINTS ELSEWHERE OR NOWHERE.** The file writes the estate's own coverage literal into itself; no row cites it.

**CONTROL ON THE DISCRIMINATOR** -- of the cited paths that exist, **175 carry an id and 11 do not**, so carrying one is the norm for a real witness and its absence in the orphan set is informative rather than an artefact of the pattern.

**WHAT THE 36 ARE NOT:** L3 requires a CITED file to carry its row's id. It does not require every file carrying an id to be cited, and several files may legitimately carry the same one. So 36 is a CANDIDATE population that a human must disposition, not a defect count either.

## A CORRECTION TO THE PREMISE THIS ROW WAS RAISED ON

**The other direction was reported to me as gated and reporting 37 absent. The 37 is real and I reproduced it exactly -- but it is NOT a defect count, and reading it as one overstates the estate's debt.**

| the 37 cited paths that do not exist | status of the citing row |
| --- | --- |
| 36 | **`to-write`** |
| 1 | `fiat` |
| **0** | **`green`** |

**A `to-write` row citing a file that does not exist yet is CORRECT.** That is what `to-write` means. Driven: `intent at lint` is clean on **every** ST in the estate, including ST0056, which carries 21 of the 37.

So the asymmetry is sharper than "one end is gated": **the gated direction currently reports ZERO defects, and the ungated direction has never been counted at all.**

## A NEGATIVE RESULT, RECORDED SO NOBODY RE-RUNS IT

I tried to promote the 36 into something stronger -- *work already done while canon still records it `to-write`* -- by matching ids declared in orphan files against `to-write` rows. **IT DOES NOT SURVIVE.** AT ids are per-thread and collide across threads: an orphan carrying `AT-01.1` matches ST0046's `AT-01.1` by coincidence of numbering, not by subject. The output is dominated by that collision and establishes nothing.

**AND THE QUESTION ALREADY HAS AN OWNER**, found by searching before filing: `stale_at_check.sh` -- *catches UNDERSTATEMENT: a `to-write` row whose cited test already exists*. Its mirror `absent_at_check.sh` catches the overstatement. **Neither covers the orphan direction**, because both start from a ROW. Every instrument in this space does. That is the structural reason the gap exists and it is the thing a fix has to change.

## WHAT WOULD CLOSE THIS

An instrument that starts from the ARTEFACT rather than the row, reporting the orphan set with the id-carrying sub-population separated, so a human dispositions 36 rather than 151. It is a census, not a gate: **gating it would be wrong today**, because most orphans are legitimately uncited and a red gate on 151 would be turned off within a day.

Raised by ic, confirmed independently by vc before it was assigned. Searched before filing (`orphaned test file no acceptance row cites`, `existing-to-cited direction`, `test file cited by nothing`, `AC-00.16`, `orphan`): `0264` is a different subject (`dist-provenance.txt`'s two readers), and the parity tools above are the near neighbours, all row-first.



## DISPOSITIONED (ic, 2026-09-05, on vc's assignment). **MY OWN DISCRIMINATOR WAS WRONG BY 3x, IN THE DIRECTION THAT FLATTERED THE ROW.**

**THE 36 IS NOT THE POPULATION. IT IS 13.** The L3 cut counts a file as claiming coverage if it contains an `AT-NN.N`. **It cannot tell a CLAIM from a STRING**, and three separate classes of string are in there:

| class | dropped | the proof |
| --- | --- | --- |
| the id is FIXTURE DATA constructed in code | 16 | `store_round_trip.rs:107` -- `id: "AT-99.1".to_string()`. **`AT-99.1` and `AT-30.1` exist in NO canon file**; `AT-30.1` sits in a fixture row whose status is `chartreuse`, deliberately invalid |
| the id belongs to ANOTHER ESTATE, quoted verbatim as migration provenance | 6 | `legacy_citation_and_prose_covers.rs:53` -- *Captured verbatim from `Arca/arca_cli` `ST0011` AT-07.1*. `legacy_covers_plus.rs:88` -- *Lamplight `ST0257 AT-13.1`, verbatim* |
| the whole `legacy_*` family | (above) | **it is the v2-MIGRATION test corpus, so its AT ids are other estates' canon BEING CONVERTED.** That is a rule, not a list |

**THE WORKING DISCRIMINATOR IS WHETHER THE ID APPEARS IN A COMMENT OR ONLY IN CODE**, and the strongest form of the claim is a `//!` module doc opening with the id -- a file declaring in its first line which row it witnesses.

**THIS IS THE SAME DEFECT I CORRECTED IN THE PREMISE HANDED TO ME, COMMITTED BY MY OWN INSTRUMENT ONE SECTION EARLIER.** The 36 was arithmetically right and counted the wrong noun. **A discriminator taken from the estate's own mechanism is not thereby a measurement of what you want** -- L3 constrains what a CITED file must contain, and I read it backwards as a test of what an UNCITED file means.

### The population, dispositioned

**13 files declare one of THIS estate's rows in a comment and are cited by nobody.** Two instances are worth acting on and the rest are second witnesses to rows already cited elsewhere -- legitimate, and invisible.

**INSTANCE 1 -- `AT-17.6` IS THE ROW THIS WHOLE ISSUE IS ABOUT, AND ALL THREE INSTRUMENTS ARE BLIND TO IT FOR THREE DIFFERENT REASONS.**

    ST0056  AT-17.6   status=to-write   file=NONE
    native/rust/crates/intent-cli/tests/edit_and_browse_reach_one_model.rs:1
      //! `AT-17.6` / `AC-17.6`: **`intent edit <kind> <id>` and `intent browse <kind> <id>`
      //! reach ONE MODEL through ONE SERVICE.**

**The row says no test is written. A file opens by declaring itself that row's witness.** `common/mod.rs:825` references the same row.

- `stale_at_check.sh` catches a `to-write` row whose CITED test exists -- **this row cites nothing**, so there is no path to check.
- `absent_at_check.sh` catches a `green`/`red` row citing an absent file -- **this row is `to-write`**.
- `declared_kind_check.sh` checks agreement AT THE DECLARED PATH -- **there is no declared path**.

**A ROW WITH NO CITATION IS THE BLIND SPOT OF EVERY ROW-FIRST INSTRUMENT SIMULTANEOUSLY**, because all three of them start by reading a path off the row. That is this issue's thesis with a name attached, and it is stronger evidence than the census.

**NOT ACTED ON**: `AC-17.6`'s open limb is live territory under a vc ruling (DO NOT START). Naming the citation gap is a measurement; repairing the row is not mine this turn.

**INSTANCE 2 -- a green row cites a SOURCE file, and a real test file claiming the same row is orphaned.** `AT-17.10` is `green` citing `crates/intent-cli/src/tui/edit.rs` -- **legitimate, checked rather than assumed**: that file carries 9 test attributes and the id, so it is a colocated test module. Meanwhile `the_editor_gets_the_model_bytes.rs` opens `//! AT-17.10 / AC-17.10` and is cited by nothing. **A second witness that no surface knows exists.** Not a defect; exactly the thing this row says nothing can see.

### What survives for whoever builds the census

**COUNT COMMENTS, NOT OCCURRENCES; EXCLUDE THE `legacy_*` MIGRATION CORPUS BY RULE; AND THE ROWS WORTH SURFACING ARE THE ONES WITH NO `file` AT ALL**, because those are simultaneously invisible to every instrument the estate has.
